say: I've been volunteering here forty years. I've never had a week like this one.
Somebody tell the owner. Oh. It's you. Well, I'm telling you.
@how_are_things

options.text: I'm sorry. What would make it better?
It's an old building. Bear with us.
Rinks are hard. Take it or leave it.

say: {event}! I'm on the door. Clipboard says I'm on the door. Clipboard is law.
Fifty-fifty! Half for you, half for the kids! Oh, it's you. Still, half for the kids.
Lovely event. I've got my clipboard, my thermos and my squares. We're set.

options.text: How's it going?
Thanks for all you do.

say: Early bird gets the clipboard. And the good parking spot.
Morning! Somebody has to unlock the hall. That somebody is me.

options.text: Good to see you anyway.

say: {owner}! You've done right by this place. I'll put it in the minutes.
There you are. Come help me count the 50/50. Just kidding. Unless you want to.

options.text: Good to see you too, {known_as}.

say: @how_are_things
What can I do for you? I'm very busy. I'm always busy. Happy to help.
Clipboard's full but I've always got a minute.

options.text: Why do you volunteer?
What brings you to the rink?
What do you make of the rink?
What's the latest from the committee?
What would make this place better for you?
Take care.

say: Somebody has to. That somebody is usually me.
I've done the door, the clock, the canteen, the 50/50. I'm the backup for everything.
For the kids. For the town. And the squares in the hall afterwards.

options.text: This place couldn't run without you.
Tell me a bit about yourself.
Glad you come.
Good to know you, {known_as}.

say: Nowhere to count the 50/50. I do it in the washroom. Don't tell anyone.
The building's tired. So am I. We get along.
@ice

options.text: The ice has been better lately, hasn't it?
Noticed the work on the building?
Fair enough. We're working on it.

say: Lovely ice. The visiting teams will notice.
Good ice. We'll run on time tonight. Maybe.

options.text: Glad it shows.

say: The lobby's lovely now. I'll put it in the minutes.
Somebody fixed the hall. We had squares in it. Very civilised.

options.text: That's the idea.

say: Bud Mulroney's 50/50 bought the booster club a fridge. He talks about that fridge like it's a grandchild.
Bob Ferreira wants the Peewee Tournament on time. He has a pocket watch. He uses it.

options.text: Ha. Good to know.

say: A little room for the volunteers. A table, a lock, a kettle. That's all.
A cupboard that locks, for the 50/50 float and the clipboards. And a kettle. Please.

options.text: I'll see what I can do.
Can't promise anything, but noted.
You're not the first to say it. It's on the list.

say: Right. Back to the door.
Off I go. The 50/50 doesn't sell itself.
